    @classmethod
    def create(cls, markdown: "Markdown", token: Token) -> "MarkdownElement":
        style = str(token.attrs.get("style" "")) or ""

        justify: JustifyMethod

            justify = "right"
        elif "text-align:center" in style:
            justify = "center"
        elif "text-align:left" in style:

Yes! `style = str(token.attrs.get("style" "")) or ""` is definitely wrong. It should be `token.attrs.get("style", "")`.
The current code is calling `get` with one argument `"style" ""` which is just `"style"`. No, wait. `"style" ""` is string concatenation in Python!
`"style" ""` is `"style"`.
So `token.attrs.get("style")` is called. If "style" is not in `token.attrs`, it returns `None`.
Then `str(None)` is `"None"`.
Then `"None" or ""` is `"None"`.
Then `"text-align:right" in "None"` is `False`.

So it will always go to the `else` block and set `justify = "default"`.

Wait, if `token.attrs.get("style")` returns `None`, then `str(None)` is `"None"`.
If `token.attrs.get("style")` returns a string, then `str(string)` is the string.

But the intention was probably `token.attrs.get("style", "")`.

`style = str(token.attrs.get("style" "")) or ""`
If `token.attrs` is a dict, `token.attrs.get("style" "")` is `token.attrs.get("style")`.
If "style" is not present, it returns `None`.
`str(None)` is `"None"`.
`"None" or ""` is `"None"`.
Then it checks if `"text-align:right" in "None"`, which is `False`.

If "style" is present, e.g., `"text-align:right"`, then `token.attrs.get("style")` is `"text-align:right"`.
`str("text-align:right")` is `"text-align:right"`.
`"text-align:right" or ""` is `"text-align:right"`.
Then `"text-align:right" in "text-align:right"` is `True`.

So it actually works if "style" is present! But it's very weirdly written.
